subject: SentryBridge — Data classification mapping + requested evidence
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sentrybridge.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@sentrybridge.com
Date: 2029-06-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask: data classification mapping and artifacts for SOC2/ISO/SIG review

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Wednesday. As we prep our RFP pack, we need a concise mapping between your data classification scheme and the controls in SOC 2 (CC1-CC7), ISO 27001 (Annex A), and the SIG questionnaire sections. Specifically we need:

- The canonical data classification labels you use (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) and a short definition for each.
- Where each class maps to controls for encryption-at-rest, encryption-in-transit, data retention/ERASURE, and access provisioning (role-based, privileged accounts).
- A handful of representative artifacts (e.g., screenshots of the classification tagging UI, a sample retention policy, evidence of encryption keys backing up at rest).

Can you send the mapping and artifacts by EOD Tuesday (2029-06-11)? Our procurement team will bundle into the RFP response. If anything needs redaction or a mutual NDA, flag it and we’ll escalate.

Best,
Elena
Sr. Security Program Manager
SentryBridge Financial

---
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sentrybridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-06-09T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: data classification mapping and artifacts for SOC2/ISO/SIG review

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a mapping and an evidence package within your timeline. Quick alignment from our side:

What we will provide by EOD Tuesday (2029-06-11):
- A single-sheet mapping (redwood_control_map_v1.xlsx) that pairs our classification labels to SOC 2, ISO 27001 Annex A controls, and SIG sections.
- Data classification policy (data-classification-policy.pdf) with the tagging ontology and example workflows.
- A small evidence bundle (evidence-bundle-20290611.zip) containing: screenshots of classification UI (redacted), sample retention policy excerpt, a sanitized KMS key metadata export, and our SOC 2 report (SOC2_report_2028.pdf).
- Short narrative (one page) answering your specific asks on encryption-at-rest, transit, retention, and RBAC provisioning.

Notes / exceptions:
- For encryption key provenance we can share KMS metadata and rotation logs but not private key material; if you need full key attestation we’ll coordinate with our infra team (may require an NDA and longer turnaround).
- Any screenshots with customer-identifying data will be redacted; we’ll mark redactions clearly.

Kimberly, Marissa — looping you for file assemble and a quick QA pass before we send.

Elena — will share the Drive link once the package is staged. If you prefer a short walkthrough of the artifacts we can schedule a 30-minute slot on Wednesday morning.

Thanks,
Rachel
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sentrybridge.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-06-10T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: data classification mapping and artifacts for SOC2/ISO/SIG review

Thanks Rachel — that plan works. A couple of clarifications before you assemble:

1) Can you explicitly call out where 'tokenized PII' (our wording) falls in your classification? We need the mapping to show whether tokenized PII is treated as Confidential or Restricted for retention and access controls.

2) For the KMS metadata: can you include the key rotation cadence, the KMS provider (cloud region), and any archaic keys still in the archive (the existence of old keys matters for our auditor).

3) Please include a short note about your Model Serving runtime telemetry (does telemetry contain raw user inputs that could include secrets?). We need the wording for our SIG answers.

If possible, attach the control map spreadsheet as a draft so we can sanity-check mappings.

Elena

---
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sentrybridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-06-11T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: data classification mapping and artifacts for SOC2/ISO/SIG review

Elena — attached is the initial package (also uploaded to Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq_example_shared_drive_link

Summary of what we attached:
- redwood_control_map_v1.xlsx (DRAFT): maps our classifications to SOC2 CC categories, ISO 27001 Annex A controls, and SIG topic areas. We highlighted rows for: encryption-at-rest, encryption-in-transit, retention/erasure, RBAC and privileged account controls. Please treat as draft and give us any notes.
- data-classification-policy.pdf: our canonical labels and definitions: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. Note: tokenized PII is classified as Confidential by default; it can be escalated to Restricted for workloads with regulatory retention/erasure obligations. We explicitly call out the tokenization workflow in the policy appendix.
- soc2_report_2028.pdf: redacted SOC 2 Type II report (control testing redactions noted).
- evidence-bundle-20290611.zip: contains screenshots (redacted), sample retention policy excerpt, sanitized KMS metadata (kms_metadata_20290611.csv), and an export of key-rotation history (key_rotation_log_202812-202906.csv).

Specific answers to your clarifications:
1) Tokenized PII mapping: Confidential by default — see redwood_control_map_v1.xlsx, tab 'DataClass_Mapping' row 7. If SentryBridge requires Restricted-level handling we can set a per-customer flag at provisioning and enforce stricter retention/ERASURE via a customer-specific policy (this is supported in Dedicated/Private deployments).

2) KMS metadata included: provider: AWS KMS (us-west-2), rotation cadence: 90 days for active keys; archival retention of rotated keys is 7 years (archived keys are disabled and stored encrypted). The key_rotation_log file lists the historical key IDs; any requests for deeper cryptographic attestation will require an NDA and coordination with infra (we flagged keys with 'archived' in the csv).

3) Model Serving telemetry: runtime telemetry includes anonymized batch-level metrics and service traces. Raw user inputs are not retained in telemetry streams by default; however, request-level logs (for debugging and support) may contain snippets of user input and are protected by our access controls. We included a short narrative (telemetry_narrative.txt) in the Drive folder describing retention and access controls for logs. For SIG answers we recommend the wording in cell B12 of the spreadsheet — it was written to match common SIG phrasing.

Next steps:
- Please review the draft spreadsheet and point out any rows you want us to change.
- If you need Restricted-level handling for tokenized PII, confirm and we’ll propose a mutual addendum (and timeline) for enabling per-customer enforcement.
- If your auditor needs key attestation, let us know and we’ll route the request to infra (expect a 2–3 week lead time and likely an NDA).

Kimberly/Marissa — thanks for the quick assemble and for redacting screenshots.

Best,
Rachel
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_control_map_v1.xlsx (DRAFT), data-classification-policy.pdf, soc2_report_2028.pdf, evidence-bundle-20290611.zip
